page: Amazon Web Services c8a.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 192 dedicated physical cores and 192 vCPUs powered by AMD EPYC 9R45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz with a single-thread-per-core configuration. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio with 2.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes advanced instruction set support including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16) and cryptographic accelerators such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The platform provides a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth without integrated local storage or hardware GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across raw compute and parallel throughput tasks. In CPU stress tests, the 192 dedicated cores achieved a stress-ng multi-core score of 683,823.1 and a PassMark CPU score of 183,732.71, both placing in the top 10 percent of evaluated instances. High single-core performance is confirmed by a Geekbench single-core score of 2,816.0 and stress-ng single-core score of 3,792.99. Memory benchmarks show sustained read throughput of 1,026.4 GB/sec for large blocks and write speeds of 383.09 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput parallel data manipulation such as multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 2,587.08 GB/sec.

The absence of local NVMe storage requires external network-attached volumes, making overall storage latency and throughput reliant on AWS EBS or external storage services. Because it avoids simultaneous multithreading (SMT) with 1 thread per core, compute predictability is prioritized over logical core oversaturation, delivering clean core isolation. While LLM text generation remains CPU-bound (yielding 29.4 tokens/sec on 7B models and 5.41 tokens/sec on 70B models), prompt ingestion throughput remains strong due to AVX-512 vector support, reaching 5,278.24 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models.

Given its high core count, high per-core performance, and 75 Gbps networking, the c8a.48xlarge instance provides strong cost efficiency for CPU-intensive parallel jobs without GPU dependencies. Key workload matches include large-scale software compilation, batch processing, scientific simulations, video transcoding, CI/CD runners, and distributed in-memory data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services c8a.48xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by 192 dedicated AMD EPYC 9R45 cores running at 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual CPU mapping. Equipped with 384.0 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory and 75 Gbps baseline networking, it delivers top-tier compute density and parallel processing performance without bundled local disks or GPU accelerators. In benchmarks, the instance achieves top-decile multi-core compute marks, including 683,823.1 in stress-ng and 27,743.0 in Geekbench multi-core tests, aided by extensive AVX-512 instruction set extensions. The 2 GB per vCPU ratio and absent local storage focus this configuration purely on pure compute efficiency, making it well-tailored for distributed batch workloads, large-scale software compilation, simulation tasks, and high-throughput static web serving.
